definition: A number that shows how well a team or company is doing.
exampleSentence: Customer satisfaction is the most important KPI for our support team.

definition: How much money you gain compared with what you spent.
exampleSentence: The new software paid for itself quickly and had a high ROI.

definition: Software that manages a company's finance, stock and staff in one system.
exampleSentence: Our factory uses an ERP system to track orders and stock.

definition: Software for managing contact with customers.
exampleSentence: The sales team logs every call with a client in the CRM.

definition: The department that hires and looks after employees.
exampleSentence: Please send your holiday request to HR before the end of the month.

definition: The highest-ranking manager of a company.
exampleSentence: The CEO announced the new company strategy at the annual meeting.

definition: The senior manager responsible for a company's technology.
exampleSentence: Our CTO decided to move all our servers to the cloud.

definition: The senior manager responsible for information systems.
exampleSentence: The CIO approved a bigger budget for cybersecurity this year.

definition: The senior manager responsible for a company's money.
exampleSentence: The CFO presented the quarterly results to the board.

definition: Selling products or services to other companies.
exampleSentence: We are a B2B company, so our customers are other businesses.

definition: Selling products or services directly to the public.
exampleSentence: Online clothing shops are a typical example of B2C companies.

definition: The expected time when something will arrive or be finished.
exampleSentence: What is the ETA for the new laptops we ordered last week?

definition: A list of common questions and their answers.
exampleSentence: Most customers find the answer they need on our FAQ page.

definition: Used in messages to share information that needs no reply.
exampleSentence: FYI, the office will be closed next Monday for a public holiday.

definition: Used to ask for something to be done very quickly.
exampleSentence: The client needs the corrected invoice ASAP, so please send it today.

definition: The end of the working day.
exampleSentence: Please send me the final version of the slides by EOD.

definition: Used to say that someone is away from work.
exampleSentence: I will be OOO next week, so please contact Sarah instead.

definition: A contract that stops people from sharing secret information.
exampleSentence: All new employees must sign an NDA on their first day.

definition: A document asking companies to offer a price and plan for a project.
exampleSentence: The bank sent an RFP to five software companies last month.

definition: A small test project that shows an idea can work.
exampleSentence: We built a quick POC to show the client how the app would work.

definition: Logging in once to use many different applications.
exampleSentence: With SSO, employees use one password for email, chat and HR tools.

definition: Logging in with two or more proofs, such as a password and a code.
exampleSentence: The company requires MFA for every account that can access customer data.

definition: Technology for making phone calls over the internet.
exampleSentence: Our office replaced its old phones with a cheaper VoIP system.

definition: A software version that receives updates and fixes for several years.
exampleSentence: Companies usually choose the LTS version because it stays supported longer.

definition: The European Union law that protects people's personal data.
exampleSentence: Under GDPR, customers can ask a company to delete their personal data.

definition: Written step-by-step instructions for doing a routine task.
exampleSentence: Follow the SOP when you set up a laptop for a new employee.

definition: A person with deep knowledge of a specific topic.
exampleSentence: We asked an SME from the finance team to check the new report.

definition: A way of using several disks together for speed or safety.
exampleSentence: The server uses RAID, so one broken disk does not lose any data.

definition: A storage device that shares files with everyone on a network.
exampleSentence: The design team saves large video files on the office NAS.

definition: A system that gives devices an IP address automatically.
exampleSentence: The router uses DHCP to give each new laptop an address.

definition: Tools and rules that control who can access which systems.
exampleSentence: Our IAM system removes access automatically when an employee leaves.

definition: A team that watches a company's systems for attacks day and night.
exampleSentence: Analysts in the SOC watch for suspicious activity around the clock.

definition: A policy that lets employees use their own phones or laptops for work.
exampleSentence: Our BYOD policy allows staff to read work email on their phones.

definition: Final testing done by real users before a system goes live.
exampleSentence: The new payroll system goes live after UAT is completed next week.

definition: A method of setting goals and measuring progress.
exampleSentence: Each team sets one main OKR for the quarter.

definition: A session where people can ask questions.
exampleSentence: The presentation will end with a short Q&A session.

definition: Used when a detail has not been decided yet.
exampleSentence: The date of the training is still TBD, but it will be in May.

definition: Sending a copy of an email to someone else.
exampleSentence: Please CC your manager when you reply to the client.

definition: Moving data from sources, changing it and loading it into a database.
exampleSentence: A nightly ETL job copies sales data into the reporting database.

definition: A cloud service that runs your apps without you managing servers.
exampleSentence: Developers use a PaaS to run apps without managing servers.
